newsitem.title: UK: Study finds copper in betel may cause mouth cancer.
newsitem.headline: Study finds copper in betel may cause mouth cancer.

text.p: Betel, the favourite chew of many Asians from India to Vietnam, could be causing mouth cancer because of its high copper content, doctors said on Friday.
The areca nut, a common component of betel, contains large amounts of copper, Saman Warnakulasuriya of the King's College School of Medicine in London and colleagues said.
They analysed eight areca nut products and two samples of raw areca nut and found a considerable amount of copper in them.
They then got volunteers to chew the nut and analysed their saliva -- and found large amounts of copper in it.
"The daily intake of copper in American diets averages about one mg, about 60 percent of which is absorbed," they wrote in a letter to the Lancet medical journal.

"Our data indicate that an adult Indian chewing areca daily will consume over five mg of copper per day, of which a substantial but unknown quantity will be absorbed, particularly in habituees known to swallow substantial amounts of quid juice."
They cited recent studies linking copper with fibrosis -- a thickening of tissue that can lead to cancer. If people swallow the juice, their internal organs could be affected.
They said they would do more studies.
